convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I've been writing letters I'll never send. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"There's still the matter of the murder of Grace. Nobody's settled it."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Thank you for hearing it. I needed someone to know — and I needed it to stop with you. But what do I know."
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the north treeline by the fallen oak."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Nobody's worked the north treeline by the fallen oak in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"I dreamed Heinrich was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I keep turning over the last thing Heinrich said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Ursula grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Ursula is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"The fire feels smaller without Heinrich. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"I should let you go. Be well, okay?"
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Question for you: what do you think it actually wants from us?"
"That's what I keep coming back to. A test has rules. Rules can be learned."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I wasn't a journalist. I was a librarian. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"All right —" Ruth starts to stand, then sinks back down. "Maybe not today. The fire's got me."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Nothing in particular — we were only talking."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"You want me to follow you into the dark? Earn that first."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
"This was good." They mean it.

"We never finished talking about what they confided — we wandered off it, 4 days back. 'You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is…'"
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what they confided."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Heinrich owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I sharpen sticks down to nothing. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ursula nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I should go before I say something sincere."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"I still need help with the pantry run."
As I said — Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Heinrich is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
They relax, a fraction. This is going well.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Anyway." A small smile.
Ruby nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Black Walnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
Ruby: "I've been thinking. You and me — we should be bonded. Not just neighbors. Will you stick with me?"
"Stick together, then." They look steadier already.
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Right — go on, I'm listening."
"Last time things were different. They always are." "They took you — Riddle Me This, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I show up. That's my part."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ursula nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Short version — Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"These hands? Blacksmith hands. Clipboards, mostly. Now they hold wire and wood, and they learn fast. Hands are honest that way."
"Still on what you did with your hands."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Riddle Me This. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d7: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d7: 🕯️ Heinrich Stepanov is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d7: What Heinrich kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d7: Ashanti picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.
d7: 📖 LEARNED: Swimmer (Level 1). Cross water freely. Rivers are roads to you.
d7: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d7: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Weather (Level 1). Red sky at night, shepherd's delight. Red sky at morning, shepherd's warning. It works.
d7: 📖 LEARNED: Reading the Water (Level 1). You know where fish hold: seams, eddies, shade lines. The water stops being a surface and starts being a map.
d7: 📖 LEARNED: Field Dressing (Level 1). Break down game fast and clean. Less waste, more meat, usable parts.
d7: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d7: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Heinrich Stepanov, 7 days. The mantle passes to Ashanti Walsh.
d7: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Ashanti Walsh, 53 — a Fisherman. Their hands know different work now: Night Eyes.
d7: The fire knew Ashanti — solid ground, earned at this fire.

lastSay: d31: 🍽️ DeAndre watches another basket arrive and laughs. "We're feeding the shelves more than ourselves. Not today."
d31: Ruby watches how you handle mayapple — files it away. Learning by watching.
d32: — DAY 32 DAWN — The world wakes. Animals are active.
d32: The fire burns low. One new line in the journal: Mayapple — named and noted.
d32: You wake with a start — something is wrong.
